karim: FYI plan for next external assessment: focusing on evidence chain-of-custody + HSM/KMS split-access. Proposed dry-run this Friday 08:30-11:00 PT in staging. Need a short playbook for assessors + an automated evidence packager.

elaine: Good call. We should ensure every artifact has a signed manifest and checksum. Who can own the packager? Also want RBAC rollback tooling in case we accidentally promote permissions.

taylor: I can own the packager. Idea: small lambda that zips artifacts, computes sha256 manifest, signs with pt-evidence-key, and uploads to s3://pt-evidence-archive/<run-id>/manifest.json.sig. Will push a PoC.

maria: Requirements for logs: include CloudTrail management, CloudTrail data events for S3, VPC flow logs for staging subnets, ALB access logs, and KMS CloudWatch logs for key usage. Retain each run bucket for 12 months and export copies to long-term archive.

sec-bot: Reminder: previous assessor noted lack of manifest signatures and ambiguous ownership (see ticket SI-821). Strongly recommend hardware-backed keys for signing where possible.

liz: Ops note: HSM-backed signing requires KMS multi-region keys or external HSM. We can use the customer-managed key in AWS KMS with CloudHSM backing (policy permitting Sign/Verify). Ops needs a list of principals allowed to call GenerateDataKey/Encrypt/Decrypt and Sign.

karim: For RBAC, propose the following ephemeral roles: pt-assessor-s3-uploader, pt-assessor-log-reader, pt-assessor-signing-proxy. Signing proxy should not hold long-term key material — it calls KMS/CloudHSM only via constrained service account.

elaine: Also add an emergency-revoke script that flips a deny-all IAM policy across assessor roles and rotates trust relationships. This should be runnable from the oncall CLI.

ops-oncall: I wrote a quick revoke helper:
```bash
# deny all to the assessor role
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name pt-assessor-s3-uploader --policy-name emergency-deny --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Action":"*","Resource":"*"}]}'
```
Will add to infra repo.

taylor: PoC packager snippet (will land in infra/tools):
```python
# packager.py - gather, hash, sign, upload
import subprocess, json
run_id = 'dryrun-2026-06-04'
subprocess.check_call(['tar','-czf', f'/tmp/{run_id}.tgz','/tmp/evidence'])
sha = subprocess.check_output(['shasum','-a','256', f'/tmp/{run_id}.tgz']).split()[0].decode()
manifest = {'run': run_id, 'sha256': sha}
open('/tmp/manifest.json','w').write(json.dumps(manifest))
# sign manifest via KMS (envelope sign proxy)
subprocess.check_call(['aws','kms','encrypt','--key-id','alias/pt-evidence-signing','--plaintext', 'fileb:///tmp/manifest.json','--output','text'])
# upload
subprocess.check_call(['aws','s3','cp','/tmp/'+run_id+'.tgz','s3://pt-evidence-archive/'+run_id+'/'])
```
Note: will replace naive encrypt with Sign/Verify flow after ops confirms key setup.

liz: KMS policy guidance: use a key policy that requires an IAM grant for the signing proxy and disallows DeleteKey/DisableKey for the window. Also audit key grants in CloudTrail.

karim: What about chain-of-custody metadata? Need fields: artifact-name, created-by, uploader-arn, upload-ts, signer-arn, signer-ts, verifier-hash. Include a human-readable README in each run folder.

remediation-bot: Suggestion: create a GitHub project board column `pt-verified` and link GH issues from the remediation tracker to the evidence run. Auto-close once evidence link is present and reviewer sign-off done.

maria: For exporter, here's a jq one-liner to pull CloudTrail events for the run window:
```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --start-time 2026-06-04T08:00:00Z --end-time 2026-06-04T12:00:00Z | jq '.Events[] | select(.EventName=="PutObject" or .EventSource=="kms.amazonaws.com")' > /tmp/cloudtrail-slice.json
```
We'll package that into the run.
